name: Neural Tube Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Prenatal and Postnatal Diagnostic Criteria for Neural Tube Defects

criteria.description: Presence of failure of closure of the neural tube resulting in defects of the vertebral arches
Evidence of cranial neural tube defects such as anencephaly or encephalocele
Elevated maternal serum or amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein levels indicative of open neural tube defects
Prenatal ultrasound showing neural tube defect such as meningocele or myelomeningocele

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of neural tube closure defect by imaging or postnatal examination with or without elevated alpha-fetoprotein
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis can be made prenatally via ultrasound and biochemical markers or postnatally by clinical and imaging findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common form of spina bifida with visible sac
searchTerms: spinal cord exposed through open spine
open spinal defect with cord visible

pathognomonic.symptomName: Encephalocele with herniation of brain tissue
pathognomonic.notes: Protrusion of brain tissue through skull defect
searchTerms: brain tissue bulging through skull defect

common.symptomName: Lower limb motor weakness or paralysis
Hydrocephalus secondary to Arnold-Chiari II malformation
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain due to Chiari II

common.notes: Neurogenic bladder and bowel due to spinal cord damage
Foot deformities common in affected infants

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata over spinal defect such as hairy patch or dimple
searchTerms: skin marks like hairy patch or dimple on spine

occasional.notes: Occur in some cases with brain involvement
searchTerms: epileptic fits related to cortical abnormalities
brain seizure activity from structural defects

occasional.symptomName: Chiari II malformation symptoms including swallowing difficulties
searchTerms: Chiari II symptoms like swallowing problems

occasional.symptomName: Skin ulceration or infection at the site of the defect
searchTerms: skin sores or infections at defect site

occasional.notes: Resulting from upper motor neuron lesions

rare.notes: Abnormal fixation of spinal cord causing neurological deterioration
Dilation of central canal of spinal cord

searchTerms: brain tissue herniation at skull base

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing open neural tube defect
CT scan showing cranial defects such as encephalocele
genetic: Variants in MTHFR gene associated with increased risk
Polymorphisms in folate metabolism pathway genes
other: Folic acid deficiency as a major risk factor
Maternal diabetes and obesity as contributing factors

distinguishingFeatures: Closed spinal dysraphism without exposed neural tissue
Presence of cutaneous markers without open defect

redFlags: Visible open spinal lesion with cerebrospinal fluid leakage
Rapidly increasing head circumference indicating hydrocephalus
Neurological deterioration or new onset paralysis
references: Copp AJ, Stanier P, Greene ND. Neural tube defects: recent advances, unsolved questions, and controversies. Lancet Neurol. 2013 Aug;12(8):799-810.
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). Facts about Neural Tube Defects. 2020.
